summary: Self-serve. You register an OAuth app from your own settings and any GitHub user can authorize it. The one gate is organizational: orgs that enable OAuth app access restrictions need an owner to approve your app before it can touch their resources.

scenarios.label: Any GitHub user, personal resources
scenarios.audience: Users authorizing your app for their own account and repositories

scenarios.label: Organizations with OAuth app access restrictions
scenarios.audience: Members of an org whose owners have enabled OAuth app access restrictions

claims.text: You register an OAuth app yourself, from Developer settings in your own account.

evidence.quote: In the left sidebar, click Developer settings.

claims.text: One OAuth app can register up to 10 callback URLs.

evidence.quote: You can enter up to 10 callback URLs.

claims.text: Users authorize an OAuth app, and it then acts as the authenticated user.

evidence.quote: users authorize OAuth apps, which gives the app the ability to act as the authenticated user.

claims.text: GitHub says GitHub Apps are generally preferred over OAuth apps.

evidence.quote: In general, GitHub Apps are preferred over OAuth apps.

claims.text: If an organization enables OAuth app access restrictions, members must get an organization owner's approval before your app can access that org's resources.

evidence.quote: When OAuth app access restrictions are enabled, organization members and outside collaborators must request approval

steps.title: Decide: OAuth app or GitHub App
steps.detail: OAuth apps act as the user with scope-based access; GitHub Apps get fine-grained permissions. This guide covers the OAuth app path, which is what an OAuth2 auth config in Composio expects.

steps.title: Register a new OAuth app
steps.detail: Profile picture, then Settings, then Developer settings, then OAuth apps, then New OAuth App. Enter the app name and homepage URL.

steps.title: Set the callback URL to Composio's
steps.detail: Paste the redirect URI shown when you create a custom auth config in the Composio dashboard. You can add up to 10 callback URLs if you also need local or staging ones.

steps.title: Generate a client secret and create the Composio auth config
steps.detail: Generate a client secret, then in Composio choose GitHub, OAuth2, 'Use your own developer credentials', and paste the client ID and secret. Keep the secret out of code and chat.

steps.title: Write the org-approval note for your users
steps.detail: Users in restricted orgs will hit an approval request. A short help-page note tells them what to ask their owner for.
steps.agent_prompt: Write a 120-word help-center note for users whose GitHub organization blocks our OAuth app. Explain that an org owner must approve the app under Settings > Third-party access, what data it reads, and how to request approval from the authorization screen.

blockers.symptom: A user authorizes the app but can't see their organization's repositories
blockers.fix: The org has OAuth app access restrictions on. The user requests approval from the authorization screen; an org owner approves it.
blockers.escalate: Only that organization's owners can approve. There is no GitHub review to escalate to.

composio.notes: Check the toolkit page for managed auth; it is fine for development. Bring your own OAuth app when users should see your brand on the consent screen, or to get your own rate-limit quota. Confirm the exact redirect URI in the auth config form.
